C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2.IntentSummary:
**What this plan executes.** The approved spec `C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2` (`status="approved"`, committed at `567ecf6`, immutable under `D27`) repairs the `--flush` mode's `--decision` path in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` and adds the index-versus-genre presence relation. Ceremony tier **T1**: one engine file and its suite, no new subsystem, no graph module, no version surface. `DurableScope` is `<None />` — `isModuleOwnableWritePath` returns false for both scoped files and no `LINKS:` header is added to a record-engine script.
**The defect, measured.** `flushRecord` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1523`) appends `selF` to `nextFindings` (`:1588`) and appends index `Entry` elements for both `selF` and `selD` to `nextIndex` (`:1589`), but `nextRulings` is initialised to the unchanged `rulingsXml` (`:1595`) and rewritten only inside `if (opts.codify)`. A `Decision` renderer exists — `renderDecision(entry, status)` (`:437`), the same shape as `renderLiveFinding` (`:1514`) — and the flush never calls it. Driven on a whole-repository copy at the spec's base `a104166b2034bb06e028598b6533c9becaeccdfb`: `--decision D41` exits 0, prints `record-flush: flushed D41`, leaves `rulings.xml` byte-unchanged and writes `<Entry id="d41" … />` into `decisions.xml`, and all three shipped validators (`validate-record-retirement.ts`, `validate-citation-anchors.ts`, `prove-record-preservation.ts`) report green. A second path is worse: the pre-write check (`:1529`–`:1531`) tests only buffer membership, never flag-versus-genre agreement, so `--decision <a finding token>` and `--finding <a decision token>` each exit 0, print `flushed <token>`, write only the row and no entry.
**The tasks, each landing its guard red-first in its own tool round trip.** `T-001` lands the at-rest presence relation `record-index-orphan` in the shared `structuralCheck` (`:1475`) — consumed by `validateRecordRetirement`, by `--retire` through `refuseStructural` (`:1070`) and by `--flush` through the same `refuseStructural` (`:1527`) — and repairs the one pre-existing fixture the relation reddens, the `C-ROOT-WINDOW` `normalising pass` fixture (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:956`) whose `parts.index` keeps `happyParts`' `<Entry id="f2" … />` after `parts.findingsRetired` is reassigned to `f9` (measured on a prototype: `163 pass, 1 fail` before the repair, `164 pass, 0 fail` after). `T-002` routes `selD` through the existing `renderDecision` into `nextRulings` in the same transaction, chains `--codify` off the already-appended `nextRulings` rather than the original bytes, and evaluates the presence relation `flush-index-orphan` over the next documents plus the retired siblings before the write loop; its red-first is reachable through the codify interaction — a naive `--decision D99 --codify d1:test-suite:…` run drops the decision when the codify branch rewrites `nextRulings` from `rulingsXml`, and the guard refuses `flush-index-orphan` (driven: naive exit 1, chained exit 0 writing both the `Decision` and the `CodifiedIn`). `T-003` adds the genre-agreement refusal `flush-selection-genre-mismatch` before any write (driven both directions: `--finding D99` refuses with the code; `--decision D99` lands). `T-004` extends the suite's `bundleMinted` payer map with `F289: "C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2"` — the trap that cost the last bundle, and live here (`grep -c F289 scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` = 0 at plan time), because `derivePayerMap` (`:370`) mints `F289` only once this bundle's row is an archive directory and the walk (`test:2210`) then expects `baseline[F289] ?? bundleMinted[F289]`, so an absent or stale entry reddens the post-archive verdict. `D41` needs no entry — `F_TOKEN_RE` mints only `F` tokens (driven: `derived.get("D41")` is `undefined`). `T-005` adds the applied-archive relation walk for `AC-ROW-F289-D41`: it is vacuously green while the bundle's row is absent (pre-close) and, once the row is present, asserts `F289` retired with `<PaidBy>C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2</PaidBy>` and its index layer `retired`, `D41` live with no `CodifiedIn` and its index layer `live`, and the row exactly once across the registry layers with `Pays` containing `F289`.
**The assertions.** `BaselineAssertions` pin the standing world with existence pins and the instruments green at the baseline — the record suite, the preservation suite, the shipped validator, the preservation validator and the citation-anchor validator. They do **not** pin the validator's silence on an orphan index `Entry` or the pre-write success line, which are the reds the tasks flip; a needle the bundle flips by design belongs in a test or a probe, not a baseline assertion. `TargetAssertions` restore every one of those instruments and add the full `bun run validate:ci`, plus `MustContain` needles for the delivered surfaces: the three new codes in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` (`record-index-orphan`, `flush-selection-genre-mismatch`, `flush-index-orphan`) and the payer-map entry `F289: "C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2"` in the suite. The full CI-equivalent verification is **close-time only**: it is the `bun run validate:ci` `MustPassCommand` in `TargetAssertions`, evaluated at `--assertions final --run-commands`; no task `Verification` duplicates it, and no task names a current-mode lint of this root.
**The full-suite-run count is one.** Exactly one command in this plan runs the whole suite: the `bun run validate:ci` `MustPassCommand` in `TargetAssertions`, at `--assertions final`. Every task `Verification` names the narrowest instrument, and the spec's close-bound `CloseEvidence` commands are the narrow `bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (the `AC-CLOSE-LINT` criterion names the root lint).
**What the authority writes, declared.** The approved spec assigns the close flush and the retire to the authority. At the close, with the bundle still under `.ngrace/changes/active/`, the authority drives one `--flush --change C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2 --finding F289 --decision D41 --pays F289 --mint-search "0 active, 0 archive"` through the repaired verb, writing `findings.xml`, `rulings.xml`, `decisions.xml` and `registry.xml`; then the gate apply renames the bundle into `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2/`; then `--retire` writes `findings.xml`, `findings-retired.xml`, `rulings.xml`, `rulings-retired.xml`, `registry.xml`, `registry-retired.xml` and `decisions.xml`. Those seven record files are in `ObservedWriteScope` (`F285`). `decisions.md` is the stub and is not written; `record-inventory.json` is `--split`'s artifact and is not written by the flush or by `--retire` (`decisions.md` is also deliberately absent from `ObservedWriteScope` per the plan-stage rule). The buffer `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` is read, never written; the authority prunes it post-merge.
**The four-times rule, applied to this plan.** For every value a task deletes, moves or renames, the tree was grepped for its assertions and each lands in a scoped file: no token, id or path moves, the deliverable only reuses `renderDecision` and adds codes; the one existing assertion the new relation breaks is the `C-ROOT-WINDOW` fixture's orphan `f2`, scoped and repaired by `T-001`; and `grep -rn "record-flush: flushed" scripts/*.test.ts` returns no hit, so no test pins the success line. Every act the spec assigns to the authority is read back against the declared `ObservedWriteScope` above — the close flush's four targets and the retire's seven are the seven enumerated record files. Both are recorded in the plan report.
**The byte-invariance baseline** for every diff command is the spec's base commit `a104166b2034bb06e028598b6533c9becaeccdfb`; every diff sees tracked paths only (`F174`), and every archive diff excludes this bundle's own close arrival. Any new test that walks the real record runs under `bun run test` (`bun test --timeout=0`); **no per-test timeout number is pinned**. When this plan names a tag or attribute form it writes character data with entities (`<`, `>`, `&`) and never paraphrases the brackets away.

T-001.Title: Land the index-versus-genre presence relation `record-index-orphan` in the shared structural check, consumed by the validator, `--retire` and `--flush`, and repair the `C-ROOT-WINDOW` fixture it reddens

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: on an isolated fixture root carrying a planted index `Entry` whose id has no `Finding`/`Decision` in either layer of its pair (for example `<Entry id="d-orphan" token="D-ORPHAN" genre="decision" layer="live" />` with no such `Decision` in `rulings.xml` or `rulings-retired.xml`), `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts <record>` currently exits 0; after the change it exits non-zero naming `record-index-orphan`, and `--retire` and `--flush` on the same fixture exit non-zero with the same code **before any write** (the four record files byte-identical, sha256 before equals after).

The clean direction: the unmodified fixture and the production record `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH` both stay green (`record-retirement: ok`), and the relation is one implementation inside `structuralCheck` consumed through the existing `refuseStructural` — no second orphan check, no new exported writer.

The one existing assertion the relation breaks is repaired in the same task: the `C-ROOT-WINDOW normalising pass` fixture (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:956`) keeps `happyParts`' `<Entry id="f2" … />` in `parts.index` after `parts.findingsRetired` is reassigned to `f9`, so the relation reddens it (measured on a prototype: `163 pass, 1 fail`); the index bytes are made consistent with the retired `f9` element (`164 pass, 0 fail`).

T-002.Title: Route a selected decision through `renderDecision` into `nextRulings` in the same transaction, chain `--codify` off the appended document, and assert the presence relation `flush-index-orphan` over the next documents before the write loop

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: `--flush --change <fixture> --decision <D>` on an isolated fixture currently leaves `rulings.xml` byte-unchanged while `decisions.xml` gains the index `Entry`; after the change the `<Decision>` element exists exactly once in `rulings.xml` **and** its `<Entry>` exactly once in `decisions.xml`, with `status="live"`, `genre="decision"` and `layer="live"` agreeing, the four live roots held (`base + headroom = ceiling`, base equal to the shipped metric read back), every written file canonical at rest (`serialize(parse(file))` byte-equal to `file`), and the success line naming a token the record carries.

The pre-write relation `flush-index-orphan` is evaluated over the in-memory next `findings`/`rulings`/`index` documents **plus** the two retired siblings read from disk (a live-layer-only holding set flags a live index `Entry` for a retired element — the production record's `d5.1` was flagged on a prototype), and a flush that would mint an orphan index `Entry` refuses `flush-index-orphan` before the write loop with all four files byte-identical. The relation is one helper, not a second implementation of the at-rest check.

The red-first for the pre-write guard is reachable through the codify interaction: `--decision D99 --codify <live decision>:test-suite:<existing path>` where the codify branch rewrites `nextRulings` from the original `rulingsXml` drops the selected decision and the guard refuses `flush-index-orphan` (driven on a prototype: naive exit 1); with `--codify` chained off the already-appended `nextRulings`, the same run exits 0 and writes both the `Decision` element and the `CodifiedIn` (driven: element 1, codify 1, index entry 1).

T-003.Title: Refuse a selection whose flag disagrees with the buffer entry's genre with the named code `flush-selection-genre-mismatch`, before any write

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: `--finding <a decision token>` and `--decision <a finding token>` currently exit 0, print `record-flush: flushed <token>`, write the charter row and no entry; after the change each exits non-zero with `flush-selection-genre-mismatch`, and findings, rulings, index and registry are byte-identical (sha256 before equals after).

The matching directions still land: `--finding <a finding token>` and `--decision <a decision token>` each write their element and index `Entry`. The existing refusals (`flush-id-absent`, `flush-id-duplicate`, `flush-row-not-active`, `flush-row-exists`, `flush-pays-unknown`, `flush-charter-f-token`, `flush-status-text-f-token`, `flush-status-closed-with`, `flush-codify-absent`, `flush-codify-exists`, `flush-mint-search-malformed`, the serializer's `record-schema-*`) are unchanged.

T-004.Title: Extend the suite's `bundleMinted` payer map with `F289: "C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2"` so the post-archive payer walk stays green

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: once this bundle's row is an archive directory carrying `Pays F289`, `derivePayerMap` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:370`, `F_TOKEN_RE`) mints `F289`, and the walk (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2210`) expects `baseline[F289] ?? bundleMinted[F289]`; with the entry absent the expectation is `undefined` and the walk reds. Driven on a prototype against a synthetic archive: `derived F289 = C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2`; `baseline F289 = undefined`; absent `bundleMinted` → walk red; correct entry → walk green; stale id (`F289: "C-SOMEWHERE-1-AAAAAAAA"`) → walk red.

`D41` needs no payer-map entry, verified rather than trusted: `derivePayerMap` matches only `F` tokens, so a row whose `Pays` names `D41` mints nothing (driven: `derived.get("D41")` is `undefined`). The extension is the deliberate ratchet and is consulted only for tokens the derivation actually mints.

T-005.Title: Add the applied-archive relation walk for `AC-ROW-F289-D41`: once the charter row is present, `F289` is retired with `PaidBy`, `D41` is live with no `CodifiedIn`, and every index `Entry` layer agrees

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The walk keys on the row's presence so it is green in the execution tree and discriminating in the applied-archive state: while no `Row` named `C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2` exists the walk is vacuously green; once the row exists, it asserts the row exactly once across `registry.xml` and `registry-retired.xml` with `kind="chartered"` and `Pays` containing `F289`; `F289` exactly once across the findings pair with `status="retired"` and `<PaidBy>C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2</PaidBy>` and its index `Entry` layer `retired` in place; `D41` exactly once across the rulings pair with `status="live"`, no `CodifiedIn` and its index `Entry` layer `live`. No ceiling value and no pre-close state is pinned.

Red-first, driven on a throwaway whole-repository copy: with the close flush applied (the row and `F289` live) the walk reds on the retired assertions; after the gate apply archives the bundle and `--retire` moves `F289` and the row to the retired siblings with their index layers flipped in place, the walk is green and the copy's three validators return 0.
